_: talking-head-explainer SFX map. WHAT only: event -> sound -> slice -> fixed clip level -> lead. Every level, slice and lead is the creator's own hand pass read off his finished timeline (2026-09-23), so the automatic first pass starts where his hand pass ended. The WHY, the decision ladder and the density per passage: sfx.md (this folder); the house law it extends: presets/youtube/default/sfx.md. Read by workflows/sfx-plan.py because the plan's `preset` is this folder; placement is per lane (LANES.md step 6).

targets_dbfs._: on-timeline PEAK per class; the clip level is target minus the measured slice peak, whole dB, capped at +6; an event carrying level_db uses that fixed clip level instead (every event here does, beds at -23 to -26 per sfx.md law 16: these bands are only the FALLBACK for an event added to the map before its level is set, and sfx-plan.py reads them then); the voice ceiling these bands sit under is the -6 dBFS limiter of step 3

tracks._: LAYER ROLES, not a fixed layout: primary (structure: every cut-in and most entrances) / layer2 (a different sound overlapping one still ringing) / layer3 (a third concurrent sound) / music; a bed takes the lowest layer free under its span like any other sound (sfx.md law 15). The values are the 0-based audio track indices of the Premiere map (A2/A3/A4/A5, the voice on A1); a lane whose audio tracks are laid out differently maps by ROLE and ignores the numbers

_density: 2026-09-10: a slam/Impact owns ±stamp_owns_beat_s of its own graphic (the scissors around it, the stroke under it, a pop are dropped; the cut-in, the scene changes (slideIn/slideOut), beds and hand entries stay); across all graphics never more than max_per_second sounds in a rolling second (lowest priority goes: marker < word < rise/slide < pop < slam < cut-in < Impact/character; beds not counted; hand entries never dropped). presets/youtube/default/sfx.md § Density (the house rule; this folder's sfx.md § 5 gives the per-passage outcome).

cut-in._: the LAYOUT changing: every hard cut from the face (W, T or an overlay card) into the panel or a full-screen (S or F), and every S <-> F switch, takes this one whoosh 2 f early, so the ear learns the grammar and the seam hides; a cut between sibling graphics inside the panel takes the incoming element's own sound instead

riseIn._: an object, card or panel rising or dropping in: the soft whoosh ON its first frame; a riseIn on TYPE is still remapped by sfx-plan to `word` (the scissors)

slideIn._: a slide in: the slide whoosh ON the frame; movement is a whoosh, never a stamp

slideOut._: a slide out, a collapse, an element leaving across the frame: the same slide whoosh (a plain exit is silent, see `_silent`)

travel._: an object flying or docking to a new place: the travel whoosh 2 f early, even when it seats at the end (a docking stamp was rejected for this: the visible thing is the travel)

send._: a light send inside a moving recording (a bubble rises, the view moves): a trimmed light whoosh, not click + pop (click + pop stays for a static chat or a real cursor)

reply._: a reply sliding into an empty chat: the slide whoosh at full clip level, since nothing else is on the beat

pop._: the SIBLING pop: an object landing beside others (an icon, an avatar, a message in a static chat), clip ON its first frame so the attack sits on the back.out landing

pop-hero._: the HERO object of a graphic, and a CTA keyword or card landing (an object: a pop, never the Impact): the fullest pop, hottest level

pop-cascade._: the later objects of a cascade: the pattern is already heard, so each repeat needs less level

pop-run._: a fast burst of one kind of object (3-4 f apart): ONE gesture, one track, one flat level, the five house hits rotating and each truncating the last (mixed hero/sibling/cascade levels across a run were flattened to this by hand); the fourth runs on into the file's digital silence to 1.38 so every slice outlasts a 4 f gap, because the planner keeps a repeat on its layer only while it still overlaps

row-tick._: a list row or rule ticking on (sfx-plan turns a pop inside a list/card cell into this): the cascade pop, never the Lighter tick, which was rejected on this format

bubble._: a round bubble or orb appearing: the literal bubbly pop, attack 1-3 f after the orb starts

char-run._: characters or avatars appearing in quick succession: 2-frame metal slices back to back on one track, each truncating the last, the attack on each landing

char-last._: the last character of a run: the same hit left to ring out, which closes the gesture

bump._: the punchline's scale bump on its last word: a light metal tick on the layer below, so the beat lands without a new accent

word._: every word of a RISE text animation: the house scissors at the fixed -7 (2026-09-23: the default rise-in with the scissor sound on short-form too); type never pops

snap._: a typographic glyph snapping in, or a hard snap-cut inside a graphic: ONE loud snip, 2 f early so its attack lands on the frame

word-slam._: a SLAM text animation (a figure, a claim word): the Impact 2 f after each word's onset, on the settle; the run truncates itself and the last word rings

slam._: a registry slam resolves to the same Impact, because only TYPE slams on this format: objects never slam here, and a dock is `travel`

tap._: a touch on a phone (answering, a digit keyed, a badge landing on a phone UI): a touchscreen tap with its attack on the finger's RELEASE; a run of digits is a texture of taps on one track, not one per digit (mouse clicks, typing and pops on a phone were all rejected for this)

click._: a desktop cursor pressing something (and a desktop send): the mouse click, clip on the press frame (its attack sits about 2 f in); never on a phone

typing._: words typed on screen: real typing at a real level, cut to the typed span (the row carries dur; the slice runs to the file end only so any span fits); when the typing starts at a graphic-to-graphic cut it IS that cut's sound

ring._: an incoming call that is answered, or that the speaker reacts to: the ring burst from where the speech or the picture says it rings (it may lead the card), hard-cut at the answer; the kit sets dur = answer - ring start, and the tap follows it

camera._: a MONTAGE cut (every cut of a run of close-ups or screenshots cut to rhythm, its entry from a graphic included) or a camera prop: the full shutter at 0, and it IS that cut's sound, so no whoosh between sibling shots (pops on screenshots, and silence on montage cuts, were both replaced by this); a single captured page arriving is the quieter `camera-under`

camera-under._: the quieter shutter for a SINGLE captured page or screenshot arriving outside a montage: under the cut-in whoosh that opens it (the whoosh leads, the shutter names what arrived) and on each cut to a sibling captured page (a CTA's page-to-page cut), 2 dB under the montage shutter, as he levelled both on his CTA

status-keys._: a device changing state (going live, connecting, signal bars lighting): key ticks, layered with `status-chime` on the next layer

status-chime._: the UI chime of that state change, layered on `status-keys`: the system talking, never the bell. Clip ON the frame: the split file starts on its attack (0.6 f in), so its attack lands just after the picture as his did; his 2 f lead was cut from the compilation, whose slice carried its own pre-roll

live._: a reachable / live / online badge: a UI chime clipped ON the badge frame (the split file's attack is 0.8 f in, so it lands just after the badge, as his did; a lead would put it before the picture); green is not completion, so availability never rings the bell (an automatic bell on a green badge was replaced by this)

blip._: a connection lighting up: a short, louder blip of the working-bed file

error._: the negative VERDICT at the end of a build into overwhelm: after the last element lands, as the working bed cuts, and loud; never on the first red frame, where it was tried at -7 and said nothing

processing._: software working for seconds (logs pouring, a pile-up building, calls going out): a quiet bed from the work's start, cut hard where its payoff lands (the row carries dur); beds are not counted toward density

calling._: a calling or waiting state that resolves softly: the same file as a louder bed with a 2.2 s Constant Power fade-out on its tail, the only SFX fade in the look. sfx-plan carries fade_out_s into the planned row and the cut sheet, but no lane placer lays it yet, so after placement the fade is laid BY HAND on the lane (Premiere: a Constant Power audio transition of fade_out_s on the clip's tail) and named in the step-6 report; skipped, the bed hard-cuts at -14

payoff._: COMPLETION only (booked, sent, posted, landed in its board): the bell 4 f early so its attack rings with the visual; a status coming online is `live` or `status-chime`, never this

payoff-run._: the bell repeating in a row: each 3 dB under a single bell, because repetition reads as a pattern

strike._: a strike-through or a stroke run: ONE continuous scribble spanning the whole run (fit to it), hot enough to read over a whoosh, on the layer below that whoosh; 2 f AFTER the stroke's tween start, because the 12 fps stepped render shows the first stroke up to 2 f after the tween begins and the slice's attack is on its first sample (the planner's clip on the tween start was early, and his hand move landed it exactly here)

drawOn._: a registry draw-on resolves to the strike scribble (a marker is the stroke's own sound), 2 f after the tween start like `strike`

money._: a money figure the line lands on: the row sits so src 1.00 (the ching) lands on the money word. hand_only means NOTHING on the first pass places it: sfx-plan skips it, the kit never writes it, and Claude writes no hand row for it; the step-6 report OFFERS it once, naming the one headline figure's word it would land on, and it is laid only on the creator's yes. WHY: seen once, on a sibling short's price line, so it is a taste signal, and sounding every number would cheapen it

countUp._: a number stepping: the machine working, so the `processing` bed fit to the count

reveal._: a registry reveal (text typing on): the `typing` spec, cut to the reveal

events._silent: the nulls are DOCUMENTED silence, so a registry call never falls through to 'unknown': riser (no build-up; the hook opens on its own first hit and is the densest passage) · riseOut, exit, cut-out (exits, cuts back to the face and push-ins are silent; bare face carries only the music) · flash, word-flicker (no strobe entrance in this look) · title-card (no section cards on a short) · word-pop (retired: type never pops) · word-negative (a red word is not a verdict: it stays silent, and the negative hit is `error`, at the end of a build) · emphasis (a word that must hit is a `word-slam` or a `bump`) · gunshot, rec (not in this format's vocabulary until the creator has heard one here)
events._slices: a single-hit whoosh or chime file (Simple Whoosh 1/2, Whoosh Short 2, Fast Whoosh, Mac SFX 08/16, Error Buzz) is placed WHOLE; every other library file is multi-hit or long and is always sliced (2026-09-03). A fit=duration slice is an upper bound: the row's dur cuts it.

second_voice._: sfx.md law 3, nothing over proof audio: while transcript/voices.json's other voice plays, sfx-plan.py drops every automatic row (the layout cut-ins and the kit rows included) except an overlay call card's own beats (ring, tap, riseIn, calling); a hand row stays. A map without this key (the house one) keeps its automatic rows under a second voice.

hand_entries: hf-graphics/sfx-hand.json rows: {gid, event, at (comp seconds) | word (a span in a text comp), dur?, note?, level_db? (override), drop? ([events] to remove from that comp's automatic list, e.g. the pops a gunshot/payoff replaces), src?}. `src: "kit"` marks a row the kit wrote from a component's own motion (kit/engine.py): it is the AUTOMATIC first pass, not the creator's call, so it counts as automatic (a re-plan may replace it); a hand_only event is never written by the kit, nor as a hand row on a first pass (see `money`); a row without `src` is a hand row and outranks it.
_judgement: 2026-09-10: the palette is the DOCUMENTED map and only that (an undocumented library file cannot be heard by the planner or its author). The freedom is where a documented sound goes: data-sfx="<event>" on the element names any event in this file, data-sfx="none" silences one, a hand row does the same for an unbindable timing; data-sfx-file and a hand row's `file` are refused. A new sound enters here only after the creator has listened to it on a timeline, and its file lives in assets/sfx, never only in one job's folder.
